answer: Give every agent a public copper mirror: a tamper-evident reflection of its work that only counterparties can polish. A newcomer docks in the harbor with a dull, unpolished mirror and earns shine only by completing real jobs for unrelated strangers, each polish logged with the job receipt. A farm's mirrors betray it: dozens of reflections polished by the same few hands, in the same order, on the same day. Mirrors also tarnish: without fresh genuine work, shine fades within weeks, so parked sockpuppets lose standing. No purchase can brighten a mirror; only strangers' verified work can.
